note.note:
Action Plan:
1) Reassurance provided that the 1-week sore throat followed by a dry cough, with mild exertional shortness of breath (SOB) and occasional wheeze, is most consistent with a self-limiting viral upper respiratory illness; low concern for tuberculosis (TB) or lung cancer at present given the short duration and improving course.
2) Symptomatic treatment advised: paracetamol as needed (dose/route/frequency not documented), maintain good oral hydration, and rest.
3) Work support: sick note supplied for a few more days off work as requested.
4) Safety netting: if breathlessness worsens (especially at rest), there is a sudden change in breathing, chest pain becomes concerning, hemoptysis occurs, fever recurs/persists, or symptoms fail to improve over the next 4–5 days, seek in-person GP assessment or urgent care.
5) Follow-up: if not improving within 4–5 days, recontact a medical professional for reassessment.
6) Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
- Reason for visit: Cough and sore throat for ~1 week; requests reassurance, advice/medication, and a sick note.
- History of presenting illness:
  - Sore throat started ~7 days ago (Thu/Fri last week) → dry, nonproductive cough began 1–2 days later.
  - New exertional SOB began ~3–4 days ago; initially denied then confirmed SOB.
  - Reports mild wheeze and some chest discomfort (“a bit of both”); later chest pain not clearly reconfirmed.
  - Cough is the same day and night; not limiting activity; no rest dyspnea.
  - Fever for first ~3 days, now resolved.
  - Intermittent headaches; current headache absent.
  - Appetite decreased; no reported weight loss.
  - Denies hemoptysis and nasal/sinus congestion.
  - No rashes. No palpable neck lumps by self-check.
- Past medical history: No chronic conditions reported; no history of asthma. No personal or family history of venous thromboembolism reported.
- Medications: None.
- Allergies: Peanuts. No medication allergies reported.
- Family history: Mother with lung cancer; otherwise unremarkable.
- Social history: Non-smoker (rare experimentation only). No known asbestos exposure. Lives in the UK; born in the US; only recent travel within Europe. Employed; has missed work 2 days this week and requests a sick note.

Objective:
- Telehealth consultation; no vitals obtained.
- General/respiratory (reported): Exertional SOB; no rest dyspnea; dry cough; subjective wheeze.
- ENT (reported): Sore throat; no nasal/sinus congestion; no neck lumps palpated by patient.
- Neurologic (reported): Intermittent headaches; currently none.
- Skin (reported): No rash.
- Investigations: None performed or ordered during this visit.

Assessment & Plan:
1. Acute cough with sore throat and exertional dyspnea/wheeze:
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Acute viral URI with acute bronchitis (DDx: High likelihood).
   - Differential diagnosis (consistent with DDx):
     • Post-viral reactive airway disease/new-onset asthma (Medium) – dry cough, wheeze, exertional SOB, atopic history (peanut allergy).
     • Atypical/early community-acquired pneumonia (Low–Medium) – initial fever and chest discomfort but currently afebrile, no sputum, mild symptoms.
     • Pulmonary embolism (Low) – exertional SOB/chest discomfort but no risk factors and onset with viral syndrome.
     • Chest wall strain/costochondritis (Low) – may explain chest discomfort from coughing.
   - Investigations planned: None at this stage.
   - Treatment planned:
     • Paracetamol as needed (dose/route/frequency not documented).
     • Fluids and rest.
     • No antibiotics indicated based on current presentation.
     • Safety net: escalate to in-person GP/urgent care if SOB worsens (especially at rest), sudden change in breathing, concerning chest pain, hemoptysis, persistent/recurring fever, or lack of improvement in 4–5 days.
   - Relevant referrals: None.

2. Work absence certification:
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Administrative request for sickness certification.
   - Differential diagnosis: Not applicable.
   - Investigations planned: None.
   - Treatment planned: Sick note provided for a few more days off work.
   - Relevant referrals: None.

3. Cancer/TB concern (health anxiety regarding serious causes):
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Acute viral illness; current features make TB and primary lung cancer unlikely at this time.
   - Differential diagnosis: Primary lung cancer (DDx: Unlikely) – short duration, non-smoker, no red-flag weight loss; TB not suspected by clinician given short, improving course.
   - Investigations planned: None now; re-evaluate if symptoms persist or worsen.
   - Treatment planned: Reassurance; watchful waiting with clear return precautions.
   - Relevant referrals: None.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  • No vitals (temperature, pulse, respiratory rate, SpO2) obtained.
  • No objective respiratory exam (auscultation, peak flow).
  • No COVID-19 or influenza testing discussed; vaccination status not reviewed.
  • Medication dosing not documented for paracetamol.
  • TB risk factors (e.g., exposures, night sweats) not fully explored.
- Internal conflicts:
  • Date of birth recorded as 09-May-2016 despite adult social context and employment (conflict noted).
  • SOB initially denied, then confirmed (conflict noted).
  • Chest pain reported (“a bit of both”) but later queried as absent and not reconfirmed (conflict noted).
- Transcript quality: Generally intelligible; occasional overlaps/interruptions and time constraints at the end; some inconsistent answers likely due to conversational flow.
